documents.title: Artificial Intelligence (USM AI Syllabus Policy; AI Usage Policy for Instruction)
documents.summary: The Provost page hosts the university AI vision, the syllabus policy requiring each course to state its AI rules with three template options, and promotional material on AI courses, grants, partnerships, workshops and the AI Taskforce.
documents.stance_why: The page says 'Each instructor will determine the permitted use of artificial intelligence in each course' and gives three syllabus options (Encouraged Use, Permissible Use, Human-Generated Work Only), so the university sets no stance itself.

units.why: The vision says the university 'relies on the disciplinary expertise of our faculty to guide students' on appropriate use, so the university sets no rule and hands the decision to faculty; P04 fits because the decision sits with faculty.
units.anchor: relies on the disciplinary expertise of our faculty to guide students

units.why: The vision states the aim that students develop 'critical thinking, curiosity, and ethical questioning' when engaging with AI; this is a principles statement, so P56 (institution-wide purpose and principles) rather than a skill-building rule.
units.anchor: develop and hone their capacity for critical thinking, curiosity, and ethical questioning

units.why: The vision says students should 'be prepared to succeed in their chosen disciplines and professional ambitions', a careers rationale for engaging with AI; P44 fits the claim that AI readiness is professional preparation.
units.anchor: prepared to succeed in their chosen disciplines and professional ambitions
units.fit_note: The text frames preparation for disciplines generally and does not name AI use as an employer-expected skill.

units.why: The university commits to ensuring 'faculty, staff, and students have access to the training, resources, technology, and mentorship' needed; this is institutional provision of training and resources, so P70.
units.anchor: ensuring faculty, staff, and students have access to the training, resources, technology, and mentorship
units.fit_note: Also covers technology and mentorship, not only training.

units.why: The vision says students, faculty, staff, 'employers, and the broader community engage in meaningful discourse'; engaging community and employers on AI matches P88.
units.anchor: students, faculty, staff, employers, and the broader community engage in meaningful discourse

units.why: The syllabus policy says AI 'cannot be used for every type of educational endeavor' and can be misused, and asks to respect varied fields; it leaves fit to each field, so P04 (decision varies by field/instructor).
units.anchor: like any other tool, it cannot be used for every type of educational endeavor

units.why: Instructors 'are encouraged to guide discussions with students about ethical use within the discipline', which is explaining and discussing AI rules with students (P66), modal should.
units.anchor: Instructors are encouraged to guide discussions with students about ethical use

units.why: The page reports that 'reported academic integrity violations have increased significantly due to unauthorized use and misuse of artificial intelligence'; this is evidence on AI's effect on integrity, nearest P55.
units.anchor: reported academic integrity violations have increased significantly due to unauthorized use
units.fit_note: The evidence is about integrity violation counts, not learning or performance.

units.why: The text says 'Uncited or improperly attributed material used by artificial intelligence algorithms undermines academic integrity'; it warns that AI output carries unattributed sources, which is P120.
units.anchor: Uncited or improperly attributed material used by artificial intelligence algorithms undermines academic integrity

units.why: The text defines 'hallucinations' as 'inaccurate' outputs of language models; it warns outputs may be wrong, which matches P31's content though it is stated as fact and not as a duty to verify.
units.anchor: outputs that are inaccurate and based on perceived patterns
units.fit_note: States the problem only, with no instruction to verify.

units.why: The policy 'requires courses to have a defined policy on whether using artificial intelligence is permissible and, if permitted, a statement on how it will be cited'; this is a mandate for a syllabus AI statement (P09), chosen over P24 because it binds the course and not the student.
units.anchor: requires courses to have a defined policy on whether using artificial intelligence is permissible
units.fit_note: Also requires a citation statement where AI is permitted.

units.why: The addendum is 'a preface to the existing usage level options (full usage, limited or outline usage, and no usage permitted)'; named levels of use are P05.
units.anchor: (full usage, limited or outline usage, and no usage permitted)

units.why: The text 'underscores the importance of each individual faculty member's role in examining the policy as it is made in each course'; the course-level instructor owns the rule, so P04.
units.anchor: each individual faculty member's role in examining the policy

units.why: The statement defines generative AI tools as 'capable of generating text, images, code or other types of content'; a definition setting what the policy covers is P61.
units.anchor: capable of generating text, images, code or other types of content
units.frag_start: Generative AI tools include types of

units.why: 'Each instructor will determine the permitted use of artificial intelligence in each course' puts the decision per instructor and course, so P04.
units.anchor: Each instructor will determine the permitted use of artificial intelligence in each course

units.why: 'Students are responsible for understanding what, if any, artificial intelligence tools are permitted' in each course; students must find and follow each course's rules, P78.
units.anchor: Students are responsible for understanding what, if any, artificial intelligence tools are permitted

units.why: Option 1 says AI tools 'are permitted in this class when usage complements the learning outcomes'; a default of permission is P02. P83 (align with learning outcomes) is also relevant but the main act is permission.
units.anchor: tools are permitted in this class when usage complements the learning outcomes
units.fit_note: Permission is conditioned on fit with learning outcomes (P83).

units.why: Under Option 1 'You are required to cite usage of these tools in academic work', a duty to acknowledge AI use in the submission: P24.
units.anchor: You are required to cite usage of these tools in academic work

units.why: Students 'will be provided with examples of how to' cite AI; no existing type covers supplying citation examples, so UNCOVERED rather than stretching P25 (which is about what details a citation holds).
units.anchor: will be provided with examples of how to do so to ensure academic integrity
units.frag_start: and will be provided with examples
units.uncovered_note: Students are given examples of how to cite AI use.

units.why: 'Citing AI usage promotes transparency and academic honesty' gives honesty and attribution as the reason for citing, which is P95 and not a skill-building reason.
units.anchor: Citing AI usage promotes transparency and academic honesty

units.why: It states AI 'can enhance your understanding and engagement with course material by providing differing perspectives and solutions', a benefit claim with no rule: P87.
units.anchor: enhance your understanding and engagement with course material by providing differing perspectives and solutions

units.why: Option 2 allows AI only in 'specific instances in this course' to assist learning, meaning AI is limited to listed assignments; P107 fits.
units.anchor: specific instances in this course where you will be allowed to use generative

units.why: It says limiting AI to specific assignments 'helps you develop critical thinking and problem-solving skills independently'; limits are justified by skill-building: P41.
units.anchor: helps you develop critical thinking and problem-solving skills independently

units.why: 'Specific assignments where AI use is acceptable will be noted by the instructor clearly and unambiguously' requires instructors to state AI expectations at assignment level: P09.
units.anchor: Specific assignments where AI use is acceptable will be noted by the instructor

units.why: 'Any use of AI outside of acceptable use in the course is in violation of the Student Academic Integrity Policy'; unauthorized use is misconduct, P36. It also works as a fallback but the integrity classification is the main point.
units.anchor: Any use of AI outside of acceptable use in the course is in violation
units.frag_end: at The University of Southern Mississippi.

units.why: Option 3 says 'the use of generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) is not permitted for classwork', a ban on AI for the course's work: P01.
units.anchor: the use of generative Artificial Intelligence (AI) is not permitted for classwork

units.why: The reason given is 'to develop your capacity for critical reasoning through the use of gained knowledge, experience, and perspective'; a skill-building rationale, P41.
units.anchor: develop your capacity for critical reasoning through the use of gained knowledge
units.frag_start: The intention of this course is

units.why: 'Any use of AI tools for creation of content in this course may be considered a violation' of the integrity policy; AI misuse is classed as misconduct: P36.
units.anchor: AI tools for creation of content in this course may be considered a violation

units.why: Instructors 'should provide guidance regarding non-generative technologies, including translation and access software, spelling and grammar checkers'; routine features need separate guidance, so P100.
units.anchor: should provide guidance regarding non-generative technologies, including translation and access
units.fit_note: Says instructors should give guidance on these tools, not that they are exempt.

units.why: Instructors 'may reserve the right to send any submitted work through AI detection software', which uses detection tools to find misuse: P40.
units.anchor: may reserve the right to send any submitted work through AI detection software

units.why: 'The use of unauthorized AI tools will result in consequences deemed appropriate by the instructor'; penalties are left to the instructor, so P37 only partly (no specific penalty is named).
units.anchor: will result in consequences deemed appropriate by the instructor
units.frag_start: The use of unauthorized AI tools
units.frag_end: at The University of Southern Mississippi.
units.fit_note: No concrete penalty is stated; the instructor chooses.

units.why: The page says courses offered through MAIN are 'available to University faculty, staff and students', giving AI training and education to the community: P70.
units.anchor: These courses are available to University faculty, staff and students.
units.frag_start: We are pleased to offer four

units.why: USM 'began its partnership with MAIN', a statewide AI initiative; partnerships with outside organizations are P88.
units.anchor: USM began its partnership with MAIN in fall 2024.

units.why: The university 'established the MAIN AI Lab' with workstations to support AI curricula, a capacity investment, P122.
units.anchor: established the MAIN AI Lab in Room 204 of Cook Library
units.frag_start: As a partner with MAIN, Southern

units.anchor: provides $150 mini-grants to help members of the Southern Miss campus community access
units.frag_start: The Library Al Access Program provides
units.fit_note: A grant for access, with no statement that paid tools are not required.

units.why: The Provost offers 'AI Integration Grants' to support faculty in redesigning courses to incorporate AI; funding for AI capacity, P122.
units.anchor: AI Integration Grants to support faculty in redesigning courses or academic programs to incorporate AI
units.frag_start: The Office of the Provost offers

units.why: The page lists teaching resources, e.g. a guide on 'Rethinking Course Assignments and Assessments', pointing instructors to outside guidance: P115.
units.anchor: Rethinking Course Assignments and Assessments

units.why: The list includes 'How to Write ChatGPT Prompts to Get the Best Results', advice on prompting: P93.
units.anchor: How to Write ChatGPT Prompts to Get the Best Results

units.why: The AI Taskforce 'consider the challenges and impacts of artificial intelligence' and its advice shapes resources; it names a body that advises on the AI policy and support, P80.
units.anchor: The AI Taskforce is composed of USM faculty who consider the challenges and impacts
units.fit_note: The Taskforce advises on resources; it is not named as policy owner.

units.why: The Office of the Provost 'lead workshops on best practices for the responsible use of AI' for students, faculty, staff and parents: training offered, P70.
units.anchor: lead workshops on best practices for the responsible use of AI
units.frag_start: As part of our efforts to

units.anchor: explores how artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) can

documents.unit: Office of the Provost / AI Taskforce
documents.title: USM Responsible Use of Artificial Intelligence Guidelines
documents.summary: Campus-wide guidelines on ethical, secure and responsible AI use for education, research and administration, covering bias, oversight, privacy, accountability, acceptable and prohibited uses, training, enforcement and annual review.
documents.stance_why: The guidelines set principles but say 'The faculty will provide specific guidelines on permissible AI use in coursework' and 'faculty must approve its use for coursework', so course-level stance is left to faculty.

units.why: The introduction says the guidelines 'establish a framework for the ethical, secure, and responsible use of AI at USM' with stated values; an institution-wide framework: P56.
units.anchor: establish a framework for the ethical, secure, and responsible use of AI
units.frag_start: The University of Southern Mississippi (USM) recognizes

units.why: The scope covers 'all students, faculty, staff, and affiliated individuals who develop, deploy, or utilize AI'; it defines who the policy binds: P61.
units.anchor: apply to all students, faculty, staff, and affiliated individuals
units.fit_note: Defines scope of persons and not what AI is.

units.why: 'AI output should be critically evaluated particularly in areas like admissions, grading, or hiring' because systems reflect bias; bias concern with an evaluate duty, P53 chosen over P31 since the stated reason is discrimination.
units.anchor: AI output should be critically evaluated particularly in areas like admissions, grading, or hiring
units.frag_start: Bias and Fairness: AI systems may
units.fit_note: Also tells users to evaluate output critically (P31).

units.why: 'AI decisions with significant consequences must involve human oversight' and people must be able to 'override AI decisions'; humans stay responsible for decisions about people: P73.
units.anchor: AI decisions with significant consequences must involve human oversight

units.why: 'When AI systems interact directly with individuals ... informed consent is required' and the purpose and scope must be communicated; people must know when they deal with AI (P103) though the text also requires consent.
units.anchor: informed consent is required
units.frag_start: Informed Consent: When AI systems interact
units.frag_end: impacts of data collection and analysis.
units.fit_note: Requires consent and not only notice.

units.why: 'Individuals should have the option to opt out without facing negative consequences' gives an alternative with no penalty; nearest P51 (alternatives exist).
units.anchor: Individuals should have the option to opt out without facing negative consequences
units.fit_note: Opt-out right when AI interacts with people, not cost or access.

units.why: 'Students should disclose AI assistance where applicable' tells students to acknowledge AI use in their work: P24, with should as modality.
units.anchor: Students should disclose AI assistance where applicable

units.why: 'Faculty must approve its use for coursework, supervised research, and examinations', so AI use needs prior faculty approval: P107.
units.anchor: faculty must approve its use for coursework, supervised research, and examinations

units.why: Users must 'avoid using high-risk data (e.g., student records, confidential research)' in AI unless verified secure by iTech; data protection with vetting: P50.
units.anchor: Avoid using high-risk data (e.g., student records, confidential research) unless verified secure by iTech
units.frag_start: Data Classification: Accurately classify all data

units.why: 'Personally identifiable information (PII) must be removed from datasets before AI analysis', personal data protection: P50.
units.anchor: Personally identifiable information (PII) must be removed from datasets before AI analysis

units.why: 'AI use must adhere to applicable data privacy laws and regulations, including FERPA and HIPAA'; compliance with law, P77.
units.anchor: AI use must adhere to applicable data privacy laws and regulations, including FERPA and HIPAA

units.why: 'Limit data collection to what is strictly necessary' for AI applications; a privacy rule, P50.
units.anchor: Limit data collection to what is strictly necessary for AI

units.why: Users must 'follow USM's information security protocols' for AI data; AI use falls under existing university policy: P77.
units.anchor: Follow USM's information security protocols to safeguard AI data

units.why: Data shared externally for AI 'must comply with USM data policies, with explicit authorization'; a limit on sending university data to outside AI, closest to P65.
units.anchor: Any data shared externally for AI use must comply with USM data policies
units.fit_note: Applies to any data shared externally and is not limited to vendor contracts.

units.why: 'AI users and developers are accountable for verifying AI generated outputs', a duty to verify output: P31.
units.anchor: AI users and developers are accountable for verifying AI

units.why: Users must 'regularly assess AI systems for performance, security vulnerabilities, and ethical considerations'; monitoring of deployed AI: P98.
units.anchor: Regularly assess AI systems for performance, security vulnerabilities, and ethical considerations

units.why: Users must 'promptly report any issues or malfunctions to the AI Incident Database (AIID), any required regulatory bodies, or the iTech Help Desk', a reporting duty: P71.
units.anchor: promptly report any issues or malfunctions to the AI Incident Database (AIID)

units.why: 'Inform users when AI is involved in decision making processes' is a duty to say when AI is in play: P103.
units.anchor: Inform users when AI is involved in decision making processes

units.why: AI 'may be used' for 'generating content drafts, language translations, or creating study materials, provided outputs are reviewed by a human'; permitted low-risk uses, P14 for study materials, chosen as the closest type for a mixed list.
units.anchor: AI may be used for tasks such as generating content drafts, language translations
units.fit_note: List also covers drafts and translation.

units.why: AI 'should not be used for tasks requiring accuracy and fairness, such as evaluations in hiring, grading' without human oversight; conditions on AI-assisted grading, P101.
units.anchor: AI should not be used for tasks requiring accuracy and fairness, such as evaluations
units.fit_note: Also covers hiring and any use of private information.

units.why: 'Final accountability rests with staff' for AI-enhanced administrative processes: administrative use is governed by P76.
units.anchor: AI can enhance administrative processes, but final accountability rests with staff

units.why: 'AI must not independently make decisions that significantly affect individuals without human review'; no sole AI decisions about people: P73.
units.anchor: AI must not independently make decisions that significantly affect individuals without human review

units.why: 'Ensure AI-driven administrative tools are accessible to all members of the USM community' is an accessibility duty: P97.
units.anchor: Ensure AI-driven administrative tools are accessible to all members of the USM community

units.why: 'AI tools used for educational purposes should enhance, not replace, learning'; AI must not replace learning, which matches P32 on not replacing students' own thinking.
units.anchor: AI tools used for educational purposes should enhance, not replace, learning

units.why: 'Faculty are encouraged to integrate AI thoughtfully into curricula while preserving core learning objectives'; encouragement of AI, with objectives as limit: P02.
units.anchor: Faculty are encouraged to integrate AI thoughtfully into curricula
units.fit_note: Aimed at faculty course design and ties AI to preserving learning objectives (P83).

units.why: 'AI tools used for coursework must be cited appropriately' is a citation duty in coursework: P24.
units.anchor: AI tools used for coursework must be cited appropriately
units.frag_start: AI tools used for coursework must

units.why: 'Researchers must ... obtain necessary approvals' and comply with 'institutional review board (IRB) protocols' and sponsor requirements; research AI rules, P62.
units.anchor: Ensure that AI research complies with institutional review board (IRB) protocols

units.why: 'Researchers must consult with any intended journals and their editors' on AI policies for publication; deferring to venue rules: P62.
units.anchor: Researchers must consult with any intended journals and their editors

units.why: 'Students must adhere to academic integrity policies when using AI', tying student use to existing policies: P77 (not P45, which treats AI as a collaborator).
units.anchor: Students must adhere to academic integrity policies when using AI

units.why: 'The faculty will provide specific guidelines on permissible AI use in coursework', so faculty decide: P04.
units.anchor: The faculty will provide specific guidelines on permissible AI use in coursework

units.why: 'AI should complement, not substitute, critical thinking and problem-solving' says AI must not replace student thinking: P32.
units.anchor: AI should complement, not substitute, critical thinking and problem-solving

units.why: 'AI must not be used for illegal, unethical, or policy violating activities' is a conduct rule against malicious use: P74.
units.anchor: AI must not be used for illegal, unethical, or policy violating activities

units.why: 'AI tools must not be used to access or manipulate data without authorization', a security conduct ban: P74.
units.anchor: AI tools must not be used to access or manipulate data without authorization

units.why: 'AI generated content that violates intellectual property rights is prohibited' concerns ownership and IP of outputs: P52.
units.anchor: AI generated content that violates intellectual property rights is prohibited
units.fit_note: Headed 'Plagiarism' but the text speaks of IP violation.

units.why: 'Unauthorized surveillance of students or staff using AI is not permitted'; no type covers a ban on AI surveillance, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Unauthorized surveillance of students or staff using AI is not permitted
units.uncovered_note: AI must not be used for unauthorized surveillance of students or staff.

units.why: 'AI systems reinforcing biases or discrimination must be corrected through regular assessments and mitigation strategies' monitors systems for bias: P98.
units.anchor: AI systems reinforcing biases or discrimination must be corrected through regular assessments

units.why: Generative AI in accreditation 'should be done by users who are familiar with the concepts and constraints' per SACSCOC guidelines; a rule for accreditation work fits no type, so UNCOVERED.
units.anchor: Use of generative AI in accreditation should be done by users who are familiar
units.uncovered_note: Generative AI in accreditation work should be used by people who understand it and follow SACSCOC's guidelines.

units.why: 'Training on the ethical and secure use of AI is the responsibility of each AI user and should be completed before using AI tools' sets a training expectation: P70.
units.anchor: Training on the ethical and secure use of AI is the responsibility

units.why: The university 'may from time to time provide workshops through ... the Center for Faculty Development' and people are encouraged to take training; faculty support and training: P63.
units.anchor: The university may from time to time provide workshops
units.fit_note: Open to students and staff as well as faculty (P70).

units.why: Violators 'may be subject to disciplinary action, up to and including suspension, expulsion, and/or termination'; stated sanctions: P37.
units.anchor: may be subject to disciplinary action, up to and including suspension, expulsion, and/or termination
units.fit_note: Gives a range of possible sanctions and no fixed penalties.

units.why: External contractors who violate 'may be held in breach of contract' and face contractual penalties; a sanction for external parties: P37.
units.anchor: may be held in breach of contract
units.frag_start: External Entities: Any external entity, contractor,
units.fit_note: Concerns external entities and not students.

units.why: 'These guidelines will be reviewed annually' states a regular review cycle: P54.
units.anchor: These guidelines will be reviewed annually

units.why: 'Community feedback is encouraged for continuous improvement' invites feedback to the policy: P54.
units.anchor: encouraged for continuous improvement

units.why: Questions go to 'The Office of Information Technology Services (iTech)', naming the office responsible for the guidelines: P80.
units.anchor: The Office of Information Technology Services (iTech)
units.fit_note: Names a contact office, not an enforcing body.

units.why: The document history states '2025-01-31 - Initial publication', giving the policy's adoption date: P84.
units.anchor: 2025-01-31 - Initial publication.
units.fit_note: Gives only a date, not the process or body.
